summary:
THE BEHAVIOUR IS SOUND AND THE PROSE IS NOT. I drove 187 cells, one fresh subprocess each, through a real spine.assemble.build: all eleven domains behave exactly as declared at both endpoints and at every float neighbour the brief named -- 0.0, -0.0, 0.9999999999999999, 1.0, 1.0000000000000002, 1.9999999999999998, 2.0, 2.0000000000000004, -5e-324, -1e-320, +1e-320, nan, inf, -inf, 1e26. No off-by-one-endpoint anywhere, every refusal names the generated environment name and the value at the first read, the shipped default and both endpoints build on every one of the eleven. Their load-bearing-without-the-floor claim reproduces exactly (33 of 33 refused with REFUSE_NON_FINITE_FLOAT=False in a copy outside the repo; four no-pair FAB floats resolve nan/inf/-inf in the same build). Their repro scripts still exist and still run, which the brief warned they might not. The suite at HEAD is FULLY GREEN and I ran it: ownership 15+70, contract 16+77, census 8, assemble 9, couplings 4, fabric 9, derive 575 oracle cases 0 mismatches.

THE HEADLINE CLAIM IS HALF-VERIFIED. FAB_DISCOVER's ceiling of 2.0 is RIGHT and I confirmed it from the reader: fabric/api.py::_ground_update compares `1.0 - best` where best is the max dot of a unit centroid row with a MEAN of unit signatures, so the quantity runs on [0, 2]; measured independently, 1.4459 over 20000 draws of the api's own expression and exactly 2.0 at the anti-parallel limit, so a hi of 1.0 would have refused a threshold the mechanism still evaluates. FAB_MERGE_DIST HAS NO READER. The report attributes both ceilings to _ground_update, which never sees merge_dist; merge_dist's declared reader fabric/api.py::manage raises NotImplementedError, and an AST walk of all of src/ finds ZERO executable occurrences of the name outside its own declaration. Its [0, 2] is inferred from a stub's docstring plus the pop.cent normalisation I did verify -- defensible, but not read off a reader.

AND THAT IS THE GENERAL CASE, NOT AN EXCEPTION: EIGHT OF THE ELEVEN CONSUMERS ARE P4 STUBS. Only halt_max, pressure and discover have executable readers. cull_frac, merge_dist, new_frac, parent_max, mut_big_p, xover, lr_gamma and lr_amin have none anywhere in the tree, and their declaration comments describe those stubs in the present indicative ('fabric/api.py::grow_check refuses a parent that already holds parent_max'). The foot block's 'Every pair below is read off what the CONSUMER does with the number' is false for eight of eleven. They admit the stub once, for cull_frac, as a help-string conflict.

FIVE DEFECTS THEY DID NOT REPORT, THREE OF THEM WRITTEN BY THIS CHANGE. (1) FAB_DISCOVER and FAB_MERGE_DIST still carry U.FRACTION, whose printed text is literally 'fraction 0..1', beside a declared and ENFORCED ceiling of 2.0 -- the exact failure this file's own module docstring forbids ('a label the DEFAULT ITSELF falsifies is worse than no label') and that src/data/levers.py:521 rules on for the same number. Before the domain the label was unchecked prose; the domain makes the declaration contradict itself. (2) domain=(0.0, 1.0) on FAB_PRESSURE removes a configuration spine/derive.py::operating_population documents by name -- 'Reachable whenever pressure > 1, which is a configuration the gate answers by never opening' -- and it was the ONLY environment setting that shuts cull_gate_open at every occupancy, which is what disarms the utilization cull, the utilization spare and FAB_RESCUE together. The hi endpoint does not replace it: MEASURED, cull_gate_open(8, 8, 1.0) is True and cull_gate_open(8, 8, 1.5) is False. A prior audit had already named this fork and asked for an explicit ruling; the ruling was taken silently. (3) levers.py:990-994 is now FALSE about pressure ('the refusal that fires is spine/derive.py::operating_population's ... cannot name this lever') -- at HEAD it is Lever.coerce's and it does name FAB_PRESSURE, which their OWN finding #5 measured. (4) The newly written levers.py:1081 gives a false reason -- 'two packages' couplings reach that function' -- when assemble.py:1045 and :1136 both pass r['FAB'].pressure; the destinations differ, the lever does not. (5) Three lines later, 'the only thing standing between a non-finite or OUT-OF-RANGE number and the coupling': operating_population refuses only non-finite and absorbs every finite out-of-range value through max(3, n) and min(n_slots, n).

TWO THINGS I COULD NOT CONFIRM AS STATED. The halt_max harm figures (1.3968892609970744 -> 2.5214699913394156) are not reproducible from anything in the report or its scratch directory, and the report omits that the measurement requires FAB_SOCIETY=1 -- at the shipped default their own fwd.py prints aux and composed loss bit-identical at 0.0, 0.9 and 1.0. The direction does reproduce with the society arm on (1.218 -> 1.657). And O15 being green is not evidence about this file: its own detail line says it examines 2 of 33 domained levers and abstains on 45 refusal tests, and after discover's clause was retired none of the fabric eleven contributes an examined site at all.

NO SENTINEL WAS BROKEN AT THE LOW END and that is structural rather than argued: all eleven declare lo=0.0, every one resolves at 0.0 and at -0.0, and I found no negative sentinel among them. Every citation added opens and names the right symbol -- the one citation read for the WRONG FACT is the couplings pair above, which is precisely what O13 cannot catch. Every count in the new text checks out against the live registry (82 levers, 43 float, 11 domained, 71 without, 32 floats without a pair), and 'zero lines added above line 344' is confirmed from the diff's hunk headers.

findings.item: THEIR CLAIM: 'FAB_DISCOVER is a COSINE DISTANCE, ceiling 2.0 not 1.0' -- verified FROM THE READER
findings.detail: discover is the ONLY one of the two with an executable reader. src/fabric/api.py::_ground_update:1425-1426 is `best = float((F.normalize(pop.cent[:n], dim=-1) @ target).max())` then `if 1.0 - best > discover`, where `target = F.normalize(signature, dim=-1).mean(0)` (api.py:1414) -- a MEAN of unit rows, so ||target||<=1 and best in [-||target||, +||target||]. 1.0-best therefore runs on [0, 2] and a hi of 1.0 would refuse thresholds the mechanism still evaluates. MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY, not reasoned: over 20000 random draws of the api's own expression I reached 1.445963591337204 (they report 1.775826; the figure is draw-shape dependent, both are >1.0 which is the load-bearing part), and the anti-parallel construction gives exactly 2.0. A discover of 1.5 IS evaluable. The call is right and the label U.FRACTION did not decide it.
findings.repro: scratchpad/cos.py -> 'max of (1.0 - best) over 20000 random draws: 1.445963591337204 at (rows,n)= (3, 2)' / 'anti-parallel construction: ||target||= 1.0  best= -1.0  1-best= 2.0' / 'so a discover threshold of 1.5 IS evaluable: True'

findings.item: THEIR CLAIM: 'FAB_MERGE_DIST ... fabric/api.py::_ground_update compares 1.0 - best' -- merge_dist HAS NO READER AND _ground_update NEVER READS IT
findings.detail: The summary sentence attributes BOTH ceilings to fabric/api.py::_ground_update. That function's signature is `_ground_update(pop, signature, weights, n, cent_topk, cent_ema, discover)` -- merge_dist is not a parameter and the name does not occur in its body. merge_dist's declared reader, fabric/api.py::manage, raises NotImplementedError. AST-walked the whole of src/: `merge_dist` has exactly ZERO executable occurrences outside its own declaration (the only other hit is an unrelated field of the same name in src/domains/levers.py:464). The (0.0, 2.0) is inferred from manage's DOCSTRING prose plus the separate fact that every site touching pop.cent normalises it -- which I did verify (api.py:909 init, :1347 _entry_logits, :1417/:1425/:1428 _ground_update). So the bound is defensible as a claim about the frozen contract, but it was NOT read off a reader and the report says it was. The declaration comment at levers.py:853 is honest about this ('the pairs fabric/api.py::manage TESTS'); the report's summary is not.
findings.repro: ast.walk over every .py in src/ for Name/Attribute/arg == 'merge_dist' -> ['src/fabric/levers.py:850', 'src/domains/levers.py:464'] and nothing else. grep -n 'raise NotImplementedError' src/fabric/api.py -> manage at :2645.

findings.item: THEIR CLAIM (and the file's, levers.py:1046): 'Every pair below is read off what the CONSUMER does with the number' -- EIGHT OF THE ELEVEN CONSUMERS RAISE NotImplementedError
findings.detail: Only THREE of the eleven have an executable reader anywhere in src/: halt_max (fabric/api.py::forward, :1805/:2035-2036/:2394), pressure (fabric/api.py::build :977/:1000, spine/derive.py::cull_gate_open and ::operating_population, and both assemble couplings) and discover (::_ground_update). The other EIGHT -- cull_frac and merge_dist (::manage), new_frac/parent_max/mut_big_p/xover (::grow_check), lr_gamma and lr_amin (::own_lr_scale) -- have zero executable reads in the entire tree; all three cited functions are P4 stubs. The declaration comments state their contract in the present indicative as behaviour ('fabric/api.py::grow_check refuses a parent that already holds parent_max...', ':: own_lr_scale raises lr_gamma to the completed-cycle count'), which is a description of a body that does not exist. They flagged the stub ONCE, for cull_frac only, as a DEFERRED help-string conflict; the general fact that 8 of 11 pairs are argued from a frozen contract rather than from a reader is nowhere in the report.

findings.item: UNREPORTED AND NEW: the two (0.0, 2.0) levers still carry U.FRACTION, whose printed text is literally 'fraction 0..1' -- a label the declaration's OWN ENFORCED CEILING falsifies
findings.detail: spine/units.py:370 is `FRACTION = "fraction 0..1"`. FAB_DISCOVER and FAB_MERGE_DIST are declared `Lever(..., U.FRACTION, domain=(0.0, 2.0))`. The module docstring of THIS FILE states the governing rule in its own words: 'a label the DEFAULT ITSELF falsifies is worse than no label -- docs/04_LEVERS.md is generated from these declarations and would print "6.0 fraction 0..1"', and applies it to five multipliers by moving them to U.COUNT. src/data/levers.py:521-523 restates the identical ruling about the identical number: 'a 2.0 printed as "fraction 0..1" in docs/04_LEVERS.md is a label its own default falsifies. This matches the call the domains and fabric files made on their multipliers.' Before this change the label was merely unchecked prose; the domain makes it a declaration that contradicts itself at the same call, and the contradiction is what the generated document will print. The foot block waves it away -- 'Ten of the eleven are labelled U.FRACTION and one U.PROBABILITY, and the label bounds nothing' -- which answers the question 'did the label decide the bound' and not the question 'is the label now false'. MINIMAL EDIT THAT GREENS IT WITHOUT WEAKENING ANYTHING: change the unit on those two declarations to U.COUNT, with the line under each saying it is a cosine distance over [0,2] -- exactly the treatment the module docstring already documents for the five multipliers and the treatment src/data/levers.py chose for the same 2.0. (A units.DISTANCE constant would be better and is a spine edit this file may not make; the docstring already says so of MULTIPLIER.) No domain changes, no refusal is weakened.
findings.repro: python3 -c "from spine import units as U; print(repr(U.FRACTION))" -> 'fraction 0..1'; and from the live registry: discover unit='fraction 0..1' domain=(0.0, 2.0); merge_dist unit='fraction 0..1' domain=(0.0, 2.0).

findings.item: UNREPORTED AND NEW: domain=(0.0, 1.0) on FAB_PRESSURE REMOVES A WORKING CONFIGURATION that spine/derive.py::operating_population documents by name as handled, and pressure=1.0 does NOT replace it
findings.detail: spine/derive.py::operating_population's own comment, above its return: 'Never above the hard slot count. Reachable whenever pressure > 1, which is a configuration the gate answers by never opening -- the population then runs to the cap, and this says the cap.' That is the shipped body naming pressure > 1 as a MEANING, not an error. FAB_PRESSURE > 1.0 is the only environment setting that shuts spine/derive.py::cull_gate_open at EVERY occupancy, which is what disarms the utilization cull, the utilization spare and FAB_RESCUE together (the three mechanisms the lever's own help string names). The hi endpoint does NOT preserve it: MEASURED, cull_gate_open(8, 8, 1.0) is True and cull_gate_open(8, 8, 1.5) is False -- at a full pool the gate still opens at pressure=1.0. There is no boolean cull switch in FABLevers, so nothing else spells it. A prior audit (.rework/audits/k_derive-src.json) had already named this exact fork -- 'operating_population's docstring sixty lines below says in as many words that pressure > 1 is Reachable ... Either the therefore sentence takes the same <= 1 qualifier, or somebody bounds FAB_PRESSURE' -- and this change took the 'bound it' arm without recording it, without filing the two derive sentences it falsifies, and without mentioning it in the report. This is question 3's shape at the high end: a bound above a live, documented reading is a working mechanism removed. I am NOT saying the bound is wrong -- I am saying the ruling was made silently and the cost is unrecorded. The honest minimum is a line at the declaration and an entry in unfinished for derive's owner.

findings.item: THEIR CLAIM: 'ZERO IS ADMITTED ON ALL ELEVEN' -- no sentinel was broken at the low end
findings.detail: All eleven declare lo=0.0, so no zero sentinel can be excluded by construction, and every one of them resolves at 0.0 and at -0.0 (the inverted chain admits -0.0 because `not 0.0 <= -0.0` is False). I looked for the other shape the brief warns about -- a NEGATIVE live sentinel -- and found none among the eleven: the off switches are separate levers (FAB_HALT for halt_max, FAB_GROW for new_frac), and fabric/api.py::build's own measurement block records that a negative on this family is either inert or a reversed term, never a sentinel. The low end is clean.

findings.item: THEIR CLAIM: 'FAB_HALT_MAX ... at -0.9 sum|g|max goes 1.3968892609970744 -> 2.5214699913394156' -- the CLASS reproduces, the NUMBERS do not, and the configuration that produces them is not stated

At the SHIPPED default (society off) FAB_HALT_MAX is inert across its whole legal range: their own fwd.py prints aux=0.5077935457 composed=3.0026512146 identically at 0.0, 0.9 and 1.0, and only fab.halt_clamped and fab.halt_mass_train move. A declaration argued from a harm visible on one non-default arm should say which arm. Their repro scripts DO run, which is more than the brief's warning expected -- the gap is that the quoted numbers are not among their outputs.

findings.item: THEIR CLAIM: 'FAB_HALT_MAX ... clamp(max=1.5), clamp(max=2.0) and clamp(max=1e9) are all torch.equal to clamp(max=1.0)'
findings.detail: True, and it is the correct argument for the hi: a softmax column cannot exceed 1.0, so every value above the endpoint is behaviourally identical to it and refusing them removes no configuration. The file says this plainly. NOTE FOR COMPLETENESS, since it is the brief's 'domain in name only' question: the same is true of THREE MORE of the nine and they do NOT say it. mut_big_p >= 1 is 'always' and is identical to 1.0; xover >= 1 is every birth; parent_max >= 1 is the quota switched off -- their comments describe the excess as if it named a distinguishable harm ('names more crossovers than there are births to spend them on'). discover's own hi is the same shape (1.0-best can never exceed 2.0, so >2.0 is identical to 2.0). Four of the nine plus one of the two have a ceiling that bounds only the spelling, and one of the five says so. Not a defect -- the tree's own convention is the CLOSED pair that CONTAINS the interval -- but it is not the 'both ends fall out of what the reader does' the foot block claims for all eleven.
findings.repro: scratchpad/clampchk.py -> clamp(max=1.5)/clamp(max=2.0)/clamp(max=1e9) all torch.equal to clamp(max=1.0) on a softmax column; max of that column 0.27631306648254395.
